content:
Last week, I published one of my most successful posts.

 

It took me almost eight hours to write.
My whole Sunday.

 

Eight hours for ~600 words??
Yes indeed.

 

The post was about the disappearance of the CMO title.

 

The idea came from the TLDR Marketing newsletter, which linked to an article by State of Brand.

 

As I checked the article’s sources, one claim caught my attention.

 

It said WHOOP had hired former Nike CMO Nicole Graham.
The link pointed to another marketing newsletter, CMORoom, which made the same claim.

 

But there was a problem.
Nicole Hubbard Graham is Nike’s current CMO.
She never moved to WHOOP.

 

WHOOP had actually hired Dirk-Jan van Hameren, Nike's CMO before Graham.

 

A small mistake.
But repeated across three reputable marketing publications.

 

Then it got more interesting.

 

I asked Gemini to fact-check the claim.
It confirmed it was correct, citing those same publications as reputable sources.

 

ChatGPT Pro (not Plus) did the opposite.
It traced the story to WHOOP’s official announcement and caught the error immediately.

 

But this isn’t about which AI is better.
It’s about what happens when the internet repeats the same mistake often enough.

 

This is why a LinkedIn post can take me a full day.
Writing doesn’t take eight hours.
Fact-checking and research does.

 

This time, the effort was rewarded with tens of valuable comments from CMOs and marketing practitioners around the world.

 

Other times, I spend eight hours on a post that nobody reads.

 

But that's ok, because I still enjoy the process.
The research, the thinking, the writing.
Doing things properly, not merely for the sake of doing something.

 

I'm very confident that my efforts will be rewarded in the long term.
Maybe not with likes and followers but with valuable connections, speaking engagements, and job opportunities. In fact, it's already happening.

 

Because AI has made output a commodity.
But the process behind an output still isn't.
And smart people can tell the difference.

 

Happy Sunday everyone!
